subject: Interim SLA amendment request — cross-region failover and RTO/RPO commitments
messages:

To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@brightwave.com>, procurement@brightwave.com
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify cross-region failover SLA (RTO/RPO) for pilot

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The pilot looks promising, but our security and reliability team pushed back on the standard SLA language around multi-region failover. Two specific asks from Procurement and Infra:

- Can Redwood commit to an RTO of <= 5 minutes and RPO of <= 5 minutes for cross-region failover for our critical inference endpoints?
- If you cannot provide that commitment today, would Redwood accept a time-limited SLA amendment (3 months) with a fallback plan and runbook, plus a service credit if failover exceeds those targets?

Attached is our network topology and the list of critical endpoints. We need formal language to review with Procurement by next Wednesday (7/21).

Can you confirm whether this is feasible or if we should discuss an exception carveout?

Best,
Alex
Alex Reid
Head of Infrastructure, BrightWave Health

Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify cross-region failover SLA (RTO/RPO) for pilot

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the topology. Short answer: we can offer an interim, time-limited amendment that codifies a targeted RTO/RPO for your pilot, but there are a few operational caveats we need to call out so Procurement has the right expectations.

High-level proposal (details in attached draft addendum):
- Interim SLA window: 90 days from go-live.
- Target failover objective: RTO <= 5 minutes, RPO <= 5 minutes for the listed endpoints when failover is triggered by region outage (region-level outage defined as >30% capacity loss for >2 minutes).
- Conditions: the target requires BrightWave to participate in an initial cross-region DR run (we'd schedule within the first 30 days) and maintain the provided network peering config. Changes to the topology without notification may void the target.
- Service credit: 10% of monthly hosted fees for the impacted routes if the interim RTO or RPO is missed on a per-event basis (max 30% per month).

I'll loop Marcus and Laura to validate the technical assumptions (KV cache warming, routing TTLs, DNS propagation times) and Ben on commercial side for the credit language.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
--- Attachment: redwood-proposed-interim-sla-addendum-20270718.pdf (application/pdf)

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify cross-region failover SLA (RTO/RPO) for pilot

Vivek/Team — quick technical check from runtime/infra: the 5m/5m is achievable in our hosted environment for most request profiles, but there are three things to document up-front:

1) Cold KV cache penalty: cross-region failover will require fetching a warm key-value cache for active sessions. If session affinity is high, initial tail latencies can spike; our runbook includes a pre-warm strategy during the controlled failover test.
2) DNS & CDN TTLs: If customers use external DNS with >60s TTLs, cutover can be delayed. We recommend using our managed failover route with 30s TTL for the pilot endpoints.
3) Dependent services: any external metric collectors or auth services that are single-region will increase effective RTO. BrightWave's attached topology shows a regional auth service (ok to proceed if replicated or configured for cross-region).

I'll prepare a short appendix for the addendum that calls these out and defines the exact measurement method for RTO/RPO (e.g., request success rate / 95th pct windows).

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

- All failover tests must be done in a mutually agreed maintenance window and require 48 hours notice.
- BrightWave needs confirmation that any service credit payout will not be contingent on a separate forensics investigation (we want measurable, objective triggers).

If you can send an updated addendum with the appendix and those two points called out, Procurement will review and aim to respond by Friday (7/23).

Alex
